title: 2020年考研英语一 Part B · 小标题匹配

sentences: Directions ;
Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list A-G for each of the numbered paragraphs (41-45).
There are two extra subheadings which you do not need to use.
Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET.
(10 points)
translations: 说明；
阅读下面的文章，通过从A-G列表中选择最合适的小标题来回答每个编号段落（41-45）的问题。
有两个额外的小标题你不需要使用。
在答题卡上标记你的答案。

sentences: A. Eye fixations are brief.
B. Too much eye contact is instinctively felt to be rude.
C. Eye contact can be a friendly social signal.
D. Personality can affect how a person reacts to eye contact.
E. Biological factors behind eye contact are being investigated.
F. Most people are not comfortable holding eye contact with strangers.
G. Eye contact can be aggressive.
translations: A. 眼睛注视是短暂的。
B. 过多的眼神接触本能地被认为是粗鲁的。
C. 眼神接触可以是一种友好的社交信号。
D. 个性可以影响一个人对眼神接触的反应。
E. 眼神接触背后的生物因素正在被研究。
F. 大多数人与陌生人保持眼神接触时感到不自在。
G. 眼神接触可以是攻击性的。

sentences: In a social situation, eye contact with another person can show that you are paying attention in a friendly way.
But it can also be antagonistic, such as when a political candidate turns toward their competitor during a debate and makes eye contact that signals hostility.
Here’s what hard science reveals about eye contact:
translations: 在社交场合，与另一个人的眼神接触可以表明你正在以友好的方式关注。
但它也可能是对抗性的，例如当政治候选人在辩论中转向他们的竞争对手并进行眼神接触，这表示敌意。
以下是硬科学揭示的关于眼神接触的内容：

sentences: We know that a typical infant will instinctively gaze into its mother’s eyes, and she will look back.
This mutual gaze is a major part of the attachment between mother and child.
In adulthood, looking at someone else in a pleasant way can be a complimentary sign of paying attention.
It can catch someone’s attention in a crowded room.
“Eye contact and smiles” can signal availability and confidence, a common-sense notion supported in studies by psychologist Monica Moore.
translations: 我们知道，一个典型的婴儿会本能地凝视母亲的眼睛，而母亲也会回望。
这种相互凝视是母子依恋的主要部分。
在成年期，以愉快的方式看着别人可以是一种表示关注的赞美性信号。
它可以在拥挤的房间里吸引某人的注意力。
“眼神接触和微笑”可以表示可用性和自信，这是心理学家莫妮卡·摩尔研究中支持的一个常识性概念。

sentences: Neuroscientist Bonnie Auyeung found that the hormone oxytocin increased the amount of eye contact from men toward the interviewer during a brief interview when the direction of their gaze was recorded.
This was also found in high-functioning men with some autistic spectrum symptoms, who may tend to avoid eye contact.
Specific brain regions that respond during direct gaze are being explored by other researchers, using advanced methods of brain scanning.
translations: 神经科学家邦妮·奥耶昂发现，在短暂面试中，当记录他们凝视方向时，激素催产素增加了男性对面试官的眼神接触量。
这也在一些有自闭症谱系症状的高功能男性中发现，他们可能倾向于避免眼神接触。
其他研究人员正在使用先进的脑扫描方法探索在直接凝视期间做出反应的特定大脑区域。

sentences: With the use of eye-tracking technology, Julia Minson of the Harvard Kennedy School of Government concluded that eye contact can signal very different kinds of messages, depending on the situation.
While eye contact may be a sign of connection or trust in friendly situations, it’s more likely to be associated with dominance or intimidation in adversarial situations.

“Whether you’re a politician or a parent, it might be helpful to keep in mind that trying to maintain eye contact may backfire if you’re trying to convince someone who has a different set of beliefs than you,” said Minson.
translations: 通过使用眼动追踪技术，哈佛肯尼迪政府学院的朱莉娅·明森得出结论，眼神接触可以根据情况发出非常不同的信息。
虽然眼神接触在友好场合可能是联系或信任的标志，但在对抗性场合更可能与支配或恐吓相关。
“无论你是政治家还是父母，记住如果你试图说服一个与你信念不同的人，试图保持眼神接触可能会适得其反，这可能是有帮助的，”明森说。

sentences: When we look at a face or a picture, our eyes pause on one spot at a time, often on the eyes or mouth.
These pauses typically occur at about three per second, and the eyes then jump to another spot, until several important points in the image are registered like a series of snapshots.
How the whole image is then assembled and perceived is still a mystery although it is the subject of current research.
translations: 当我们看一张脸或一张图片时，我们的眼睛一次停留在一个点上，通常在眼睛或嘴巴上。
这些停顿通常每秒发生约三次，然后眼睛跳到另一个点，直到图像中的几个重要点像一系列快照一样被记录下来。
整个图像如何被组装和感知仍然是一个谜，尽管它是当前研究的主题。

sentences: In people who score high in a test of neuroticism, a personality dimension associated with self-consciousness and anxiety, eye contact triggered more activity associated with avoidance, according to the Finnish researcher Jari Hietanen and colleagues.
“Our findings indicate that people do not only feel different when they are the centre of attention but that their brain reactions also differ.”

A more direct finding is that people who scored high for negative emotions like anxiety looked at others for shorter periods of time and reported more comfortable feelings when others did not look directly at them.
translations: 根据芬兰研究员贾里·希塔宁及其同事的研究，在神经质测试中得分高的人，这是一种与自我意识和焦虑相关的人格维度，眼神接触引发了更多与回避相关的活动。
“我们的发现表明，当人们成为关注中心时，他们不仅感觉不同，而且大脑反应也不同。”
一个更直接的发现是，在焦虑等负面情绪上得分高的人看别人的时间更短，并且当别人不直接看他们时报告更舒适的感觉。
